children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 11 years old.

To help determine your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do contribute towards his upkeep - I help out with things like his clothes, school supplies, and other things he needs. I give about £50 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you but you're contributing to his upkeep, I need to understand the situation better:

**Who does Alex currently live with, and is anyone else already claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mother, my ex-partner. As far as I know, no one is currently claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. This is an important point - if no one is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, this raises a question about why his mother isn't claiming, since she lives with him.

Let me ask: **Are you aware of any reason why Alex's mother isn't claiming Child Benefit for him? For example, does she live in the UK, or are there any other circumstances that might affect her ability to claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure why she hasn't claimed it. She does live in the UK as well. I suppose she just hasn't gotten around to it, or maybe she doesn't know she can. That's partly why I'm looking into it myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. I need to make sure I understand the living arrangement clearly:

**How long has Alex been living with his mother rather than with you? Is this a permanent arrangement, or is it temporary?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been a permanent arrangement for quite a while now - a few years. This is just how things have been since we separated.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I have enough information now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider your situation against the Child Benefit rules:

**Key facts:**
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16, so age-eligible)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives permanently with his mother (also in the UK)
- You don't live with Alex
- You contribute approximately £50 per week towards his upkeep
- No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**The important rules here are:**

You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You'll usually be responsible for a child if either:
- You live with them, OR
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them

Current Child Benefit rates are approximately £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, and £16.95 per week for additional children. Your contribution of £50 per week exceeds the Child Benefit amount.

**However**, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex's mother lives with him, she would typically be the person who should claim Child Benefit. You could potentially claim if she chooses not to, but the rules indicate that when a child lives with someone else, you can continue to get payments beyond 8 weeks if you contribute to the child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment.

Given that Alex permanently lives with his mother and you are separated, the normal expectation would be that his mother would claim Child Benefit as the person he lives with. You are eligible to make contributions and could potentially receive Child Benefit, but this would be an unusual arrangement when the resident parent is able to claim.

**Good news - you are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex!**

Here's why:
- Alex is 11 years old and under 16
- You live in the UK
- Although Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing £50 per week towards his upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit amount (approximately £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child)
- No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important things to be aware of:**

1. **Only one person can claim** - Since no one is currently claiming for Alex, you can make a claim. However, if Alex's mother decides to claim Child Benefit in the future, only one of you can receive it. You would need to agree between yourselves who should claim, or HMRC would decide.

2. **You'll need to maintain your contributions** - To continue receiving Child Benefit while Alex lives elsewhere, you need to keep contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep.

3. **High Income Tax Charge** - Be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Would you like to know how to make the claim?
